_meta.purpose: Factors of safety for fastened joints (plan 2026-11-02-001).
_meta.decision: Owner 2026-11-02: use 1.5 for fasteners unless an FAA or ASME regulation, standard, or other citable best practice is more conservative.

override_rule: An override needs a REF-ID whose section/paragraph is VERIFIED (not 'requires verification') and a value greater than the default; the tool uses the larger of the default and any applicable override.

candidates_pending_verification.why: search for an ASME bolted-joint or fastener-torque practice; PCC-1 is pressure-flange specific and likely not applicable

may_be_1_0_when: strength verified by an ultimate-load test with real load paths
load paths from correlated detailed FEA
redundant load paths (multiple fasteners) with enough ductility to redistribute
fitting_factor.status: owner decision pending: apply by default (effective 1.725 = 1.5 x 1.15) or accept per-joint exemptions
fitting_factor.note: Guidance wording is 'should ... at least 1.15'; TFSR 3 itself requires that a fitting factor be used.

separation_factor.rule: catastrophic hazard: program FS_u; critical hazard: greater of 1.2 and program FS_y; otherwise greater of 1.0 and test factor
separation_factor.project_default: separation-critical structural joints (wing root, landing gear, tilt trunnion, battery cradle) use the fastener factor 1.5 (loss of vehicle counts as catastrophic in the standard's definition)

friction_coefficient_max.note: unless substantiated by test; not usable for ultimate-load shear (TFSR 13)

source.location: NASA-STD-5020B s4.3.3 Table 3, non-separation-critical alternate method, p. 25

preload_variation_torque_control.note: Separation-critical joints need the statistical basis (90 % probability / 95 % confidence) from lot tests; use the measured variation if larger.

verified_sources_reviewed.finding: AC 43.13-1B states no fastener structural factor of safety; no override
fitting factor 1.15 (see fitting_factor); separation factor logic (see separation_factor)
